chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, raising it (to the Prophet), said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Ali! Whoever visits me during my lifetime or after my death, or visits you during your lifetime or after your death, or visits or after your death, or visits your two sons during their lifetime or after their death, I guarantee for him on the Day of Resurrection that I will deliver him from its terrors and hardships until I place him with me in my rank.'

key_terms.أَهْوَالِهَا: The terrors and fears of the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.ابْنَيْكَ: Your two sons (referring to Hasan and Husayn)
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (Ziyarah), specifically referring to visiting the graves or honoring the memory of the Imams and Prophet
key_terms.شَدَائِدِهَا: The hardships and difficulties of the Day of Resurrection

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet and his family after their death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia concept of intercession (Shafa'ah) and the spiritual efficacy of Ziyarah, linking physical visitation to metaphysical salvation. It highlights the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly the Imams, as intermediaries who can secure their followers' deliverance from the 'Awhal' (terrors) of the Hereafter, a theme central to Shia eschatology.
